text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000002 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, but the small documented sample supports the billed levels at a typical rate, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely weighted toward multi-condition patients, and few 99215s fall on 0–1 condition patients (for example C0000110, C0000189 and C0000247). However, the 99215 share runs roughly two to four times the all-provider share within every complexity stratum, including 5+ conditions, so patient mix alone does not appear to explain the excess. Against that, the documented 99215s were unsupported at about the same rate as comparison providers (C0000131 and C0000283 were the two below billed), but 12 charts is too thin to settle the question. Some note signals are worth noting without over-weighting: repeated time entries in nearly a fifth of notes, problem-list flags (for example C0000152), a few moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab line on the claim, and no audit trail to rule out cloned or templated notes. A reviewer should first request a larger chart sample focused on 99215s in the 2–4 condition tiers, along with the EHR audit trail, to test whether documented MDM is independently supported or templated."}
